MEDSAMPLE05
Occupational English Test

WRITING SUB-TEST: MEDICINE
SAMPLE RESPONSE: LETTER OF REFERRAL




Dr G Stark
Surgeon
Department of Thoracic Medicine
Smithtown Hospital
Smithtown



17.02.2019



Dear Dr Stark,

Re: Mr James Smith
DOB: 26.10.2004

Thank you for agreeing to see Mr James Smith, who needs to be assessed for suitability for a double lung transplant.

Mr Smith presented to the Emergency Department on 02.02.2019 with severe dyspnoea and related breathing
difficulties, along with hemoptysis, fever and facial pain. An examination revealed a sonorous wheeze and bibasilar
crackles which indicated a lung blockage and mucus at the base of the lung; therefore, further investigations were
ordered. Mr Smith was started on ampicillin sulbactam, to treat a possible lower respiratory tract infection or
bacterial sinusitis and supplemental oxygen.

On 03.02.2019, scans showed pleural effusion, pneumonia, and chronic sinusitis. Consequently, the antibiotics were
changed to azithromycin, 500 mg, orally once a day, and ciprofloxacin, 500 mg orally, every 12 hours.

Today, on completion of the antibiotic therapy, Mr Smith is ready for discharge from the Respiratory Unit. Based on
his condition, cystic fibrosis, and his history of chronic sinus infections, it is likely that there will be further lung
infections of increasing frequency. We have discussed the impact of this with the family, especially regarding school,
but would appreciate it if you could investigate if Mr Smith is suitable for a double lung transplant.

If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,




Doctor
